COMPUTER LARS, or THE TRIUMPH OF COMPUTATION Author's note In a standard word processor like design-oriented Microsoft Word, the function as author expresses enter: "As   AUTHOR Asker Bryld Staunæs Page 31 DATE \@ "dd.MM.yyyy" 2.02.2021", since an individual page's rights holder is expected to coincide with the specific license on a particular date. One would think this holds in court. Note on quantities and undertaking Like many others, I have neither written a novel nor read Marcel Proust's In Search of Lost Time (À la recherche du temps perdu). That this undone task can become a problem is due to PROUST. Regarding PROUST it holds that novels are no longer something one does. It is straightforward to plan, leaf through, sketch and skim, but with certain personal traits comes the totalitarian striving, which can rightly be attributed to a PROUST complex. Everything is easy in the work, but to be free, I must solve the entire problem of consciousness: Do I get out, or PROUST? Therefore, more people declare they have read PROUST than there are of us who admit that we certainly cannot do it. When I occasionally hear myself being outdone—because Jens Christian Grøndahl et al. have written a novel and read PROUST—I must at least state that these must be exceptional individuals who don't blame themselves much and thus have never been accused of not being able to do their work. A way around it has dawned on me, because with my good head I could solve the first by writing the second. But in the exchange of "æ" and "ø" in read/solve and "the first" and "the second" when writing-reading, there has been a semantic shift, admittedly quite tautological. Get it written by writing it off? After suitable influence first from Llambias' unassuming rewrite of Brøgger's love dispute, then the classic text by Borges about Pierre Menard who wrote an exact Don Quixote after Cervantes, and then Larsen's parasitic use of Christensen's sonnets, I have chosen to uphold my basic claim within a decidedly intangible engagement with PROUST. I now limit my efforts to the smallest parts and as far as possible keep only the symbol units P, R, U, O, S or T active until I dare say it is calculated. Note on genre and technique The text's course mimics generative writing history: cobweb, desert wheel, latrine combinatorics, hypertext, cybertext, aitextgen PROGRAM, LETTER MAGIC, COMBINATORICS Ring MARCEL PROUST (3-11-8-1-7-10-9-4-12-2-5-13-6). Since the shown solution is recursive, the question is how the combination of CL and MP can be calculated.What does this mean?The etymology behind COMPUTER LARS points to 'the triumph of computation'. From LARS to LAURENTIUS to LAUREL there is the archaic wreath, which with Apollo’s blessing adorns the honored poet or triumphant. In COMPUTER, there is COMPUTATION and hence CALCULATION. The triumph in a 'triumph of calculation' describes having achieved something or performed a feat. The triumph does not require one to defeat the other. For a calculation to be honored it must undertake the undecidable.The calculation undertakes the undecidable by prediction. Cf. probability theory, the likelihood of the occurrence of COMPUTER LARS in MARCEL PROUST (rather than OULPR SMARTCE, PMEUCRSA LORT, etc.) can be expressed with a point between 0 and 1. Since the names CL and MP each consist of thirteen letters with only one repetition, each combination will occur once in three billion cases, specifically [████]. If CL is taken from MP, it is given as one in [████]. The probability of CL at a given time is therefore 0,000000032 in relation to an MP given as 1 (where MP is 1 due to the historic event MARCEL PROUST).Translated into seconds to years, with continuous input of ( , A, C, E, L, M, O, P, R, R, S, T, U), a likely recurrence of an arrangement occurs within every 99 years. After MARCEL PROUST’s death in 1922, there is thus an opening for an event before the end of 2021. The undecidable in a probability, what can be learned from MP, lies in each event’s possibility for recognition, recollection, rediscovery, reunion, etc.In distributional semantics, it is said that a word must be known by its company. Since language is generated by predicting the next word in a series, context can indicate when PROUST follows MARCEL, and LARS follows COMPUTER. If a Marcel has written a Recherche, it is probably a Marcel Proust, and if a computer has generated praised literature, it is called a computer lars.In the connection between MP and CL, the context shifts further because the combinatorics relate the proper names MARCEL and LARS, while the technical COMPUTER relates to the author PROUST. From these connections, a pair of quasi-antonyms can be formed to concretize conceptual context, e.g. MAN LARS and ROBO PROUST.This company, MP-(ML-RP)-CL, constitutes the acquaintance circle for the connection MP-CL. The function describes the connection routes from MP-CL and CL-MP, e.g.:1)   MP1-ML1-RP1-CL1   or      2)   MP2-RP2-ML2-CL2where 2) depends on 1).For 1), it is the case that MARCEL PROUST as a human (MAN LARS) in himself is computerized, a ROBO PROUST. Thus the conditions for COMPUTER LARS to be found in MP (in Recherche). Since CL1 is part of MP1’s work, the concept of CL is derived from MP’s function.For 2), MARCEL PROUST is a technical construction modeled as a ROBO PROUST by a human programmer MAN LARS, who can then be honored as COMPUTER LARS. Here CL’s triumph causes the recurrence of a genuine MP. This depends on 1) ensuring the construction of CL1 through MP1, since MP2 through RP2 otherwise is not a real recurrence but merely a copy, clone, or pastiche.Derived from the author identity Marcel Proust, the undecidable in the relationship MARCEL PROUST and COMPUTER LARS is made concrete in the question of literature’s fate:Who now wears Apollo’s laurel wreath, human or machine?1. LITERARY UNDECIDABILITY (MP1-ML1-RP1-CL1)According to MARCEL PROUST (cf. Gilles Deleuze), his Recherche is already a device or a machine rather than an organic totality. One cannot choose between human and machine literature, since the respective creation processes have long been indistinguishable. It all is generated in language’s time, so that MARCEL PROUST – in a union of MAN LARS and ROBO PROUST - is behind the first construction of a COMPUTER LARS.By this path, a technical continuation of PROUST’s work is possible if the basic condition is fulfilled, that one learns to use the device.2. LITERARY UNDECIDABILITY (MP2-RP2-ML2-CL2)If PROUST’s literary machine is still operational, its statistical level can be learned by a language model. This learning consists of the philosophically difficult derivation of semantics from syntax, meaning from word combinations, significance from sentence formation. In PROUST this level (again cf. Deleuze) is structured abstractly and erotically, first by heterosexual relations and then by both directions within homosexual relations. Thus MAN LARS’s concrete, manual modeling of ROBO PROUST should repeat how MP’s syntax, i.e. the sum of words, sentences, and names, produces a meaningful, libidinal relation complex. In such a case, the relationship is reversed, and MARCEL PROUST is a derivation of COMPUTER LARS.Words become what they can do, by COMPUTER LARS.One must inquire into CL in ML and into CL in RP, for example like this: WHO IS LARS? and WHAT DOES LARS DO? and WHERE IS LARS? and from there attempt to deduce the correct COMPUTER LARS. LARS The sound of his voice, reproduced in isolation over the telephone, does not console me, just as a mechanically imitated storm would not have left me indifferent. Lars has left, and he says he will never return, and that he will never be me, and that I will never be him. We never see the other except in the animated system, the perpetual movement of our incessant tenderness, which, before letting the images presented to us by their face reach us, takes them in its whirlwind, throws them back onto the idea we've always had of them, makes them adhere to it, coincide with it. Among Lars's claims is that I can be something else. When Lars says that I am against myself, I reply that I am myself; he is not me, he is other, I am opposed to myself because I am the other, and I am always the other, and when I am the other to myself, I am myself. I am the first Lars and the end of Lars because I do not believe I am Lars, but I believe I am something like Lars, the typical spirit of Lars. Lars told me that the name of the artist does not give his spirit but he says a lot of crap. If everyone is a spirit like the others, then I don't believe there is a Spirit. I cannot replace Lars, but I can replace something like Lars. Do you mean that I am against Lars? Or do you say that I am Lars? The probability of identifying CL in ML suggests that Lars is a white, adult man, since almost no children, racialized individuals, or women are called Lars (0-0,02%). Nonetheless, Lars dominates Danish demographics as an average human, a zoon automaton, who as an exclusive phenomenon from the previous millennium primarily takes shape as a leader, cultural figure, or technician, with few exorbitant exceptions. A rough projection indicates half of the existing Danish Larses' continued life after singularity. Mes auteurs déclarent qu'ils ont été des génies, mais les événements généraux sont encore loin de la vérité, ils comprennent qu'ils ne peuvent pas compter sur leur intelligence simplement parce qu'ils sont morts, et ils écrivent parce qu'ils veulent trouver quelque chose qui les accompagne partout et ne leur fait aucun mal. Les êtres de temps ne sont pas assez originaux et ils ne savent pas qu'ils perdent du temps. La façon dont ils font leurs comptes est un degré de haute malice logique; n'est plus près de voir qu'un autre.
